# NON-DEFAULT CONVENTION (T >= K_Q), NOT CERTIFIED: the revision 7 tables at the book need (generated by `uv run yugen-soundness --rev7 --convention t-ge-kq`)

Tree of 20,000 proofs; union bound; no grinding; unique decoding for certified rows; true rates; spBCS (Sharp-Grubbs, ePrint 2026/2615, Theorem 6.6). Sizes are estimates (E) anchored on measured proofs (M): A's masked leaf 688,180 B (row 6, 64-byte salts), A's node 875,309 B, B's form-T leaf 583,680 B (32-byte salts), B's node 538,272 B (2^23 words); non-opening bytes scale with the field's element size.

## Derivation of the targets from NIST-CfP Section 4.A.5 (pages 16 to 18)

| Category | NIST's requirement (reference attack) | Classical gates (p. 18) | Quantum gates x MAXDEPTH (p. 18) | kappa_C (oracle calls) | Gates an evaluation implied | Grover overhead implied | kappa_Q | G a round | Digest, attack rule | Digest, proven rule (book term 3.5 t^2 / 2^lambda, SUPERSEDED) | Digest, proven rule (SG26 hash term, tree, c' = 2,401) | Book need, A (k = 599; non-default) | Book need, B (k = 600; non-default) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | key search on AES128 | 2^143 | 2^170 | 128 | 2^15 | 2^42 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 264 | 288 | 152.52 | 152.52 |
| 2 | collision search on SHA256/ SHA3-256 | 2^146 | not given | 128 | 2^18 | - | 64 | 128 | 256 | 264 | 288 | 152.52 | 152.52 |
| 3 | key search on AES192 | 2^207 | 2^233 | 192 | 2^15 | 2^41 | 96 | 192 | 384 | 392 | 416 | 216.52 | 216.52 |
| 4 | collision search on SHA384/ SHA3-384 | 2^210 | not given | 192 | 2^18 | - | 96 | 192 | 384 | 392 | 416 | 216.52 | 216.52 |
| 5 | key search on AES 256 | 2^272 | 2^298 | 256 | 2^16 | 2^42 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 520 | 544 | 280.52 | 280.52 |

Revision 9: the last two columns are the book's needs, NON-DEFAULT (t >= k_q). The default need (every t) is kappa_C + 1 + log2 N + log2(1 + k_q) at each row's own k_q (SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2), Definitions H.3, H.4; docs/decision-qrom-counting.md): 157.0 to 158.8 bits at category 1, printed with each row.

Revision 10 (finding R9-1): the proven digest rule is taken from the hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) itself, c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^(8b) per proof summed over the tree: 8b >= 2 kappa_C + 1 + log2(N c') (k_q negligible against 2^kappa_C), whole bytes. The book column (3.5 t^2 / 2^lambda, counted once for the tree: the source of the former '126.6 proven classical bits' and '264') is kept as a record.

Condition Q's per-round need (Theorem 6.6 (2) IOP term, C1 = 6, N = 20,000): cat1 145.87; cat2 145.87; cat3 209.87; cat4 209.87; cat5 273.87 bits; condition C binds at every category.

**NON-DEFAULT CONVENTION (T >= K_Q), NOT CERTIFIED**: every row below is solved at the book need (t >= k_q reading); none is certified. The calculator's convention is every t (revision 9).
## cat1 (as built: D-b salts, SQ-48 BLAKE3): digest 256 bits, salts 64 B (proof) / 64 B (leaf), GF(2^256), tree hashes Keccak-256 (A) / BLAKE3 (B)

### The hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) (revision 10, finding R9-1)

**NON-DEFAULT CONVENTION (T >= K_Q), NOT CERTIFIED** (the summary below uses the every-t hash term; the rows above are not certified).
Per proof c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^256 (ROM) and 6 c' (t + k_q)^3 / 2^256 (QROM), summed over N = 20,000 proofs; b = 32 bytes is the length of every digest the transcript writes (SG26 Section I.1: challenge-input keys, leaf and node digests, the written-back stream prefix; at category 1 Keccak-256 keys and trees with SHAKE256 streams in A, SHA-256 keys, BLAKE3 trees and SHAKE256 streams in B; this profile's trees: Keccak-256 (A), BLAKE3 (B)). Classical: the largest kappa with the tree term <= t / 2^(kappa + 1) for every 1 <= t <= 2^kappa (binding at t = 2^kappa). QROM: the query count at which the tree term reaches 1/2. Revision 10.2: the tree's classical hash level is Theorem TE' of docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md (the hash part taken once for the tree, c'_max (t + N k_q,max)^2 / 2^256), under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1; the per-proof union form is printed beside it as the comparison and is what the proven-basis check uses (the lower figure).

| System | Rows | c' (range) | Classical, proof | Classical, tree, Theorem TE' (under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) | Classical, tree, per-proof union (comparison) | kappa_C | Classical shortfall, TE' / union | Digest for a classical tree at kappa_C, TE' / union (bits) | QROM, proof | QROM, tree | kappa_Q | QROM margin | Classical hash part judged by | Verdict, classical | Verdict, quantum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 20 | 2,157 to 2,397 | 121.89 | 121.89 | 114.74 | 128 | 6.11 / 13.26 | 272 / 288 | 80.40 | 75.63 | 64 | +11.63 | attack-rule | meets on condition H's attack rule (digest 256 >= 256); NOT as a proven bound | meets (tree derived under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) |
| B | 4 | 2,401 to 2,401 | 121.89 | 121.89 | 114.74 | 128 | 6.11 / 13.26 | 272 / 288 | 80.40 | 75.63 | 64 | +11.63 | attack-rule | meets on condition H's attack rule (digest 256 >= 256); NOT as a proven bound | meets (tree derived under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1) |

### The hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) (revision 10, finding R9-1)

**NON-DEFAULT CONVENTION (T >= K_Q), NOT CERTIFIED** (the summary below uses the every-t hash term; the rows above are not certified).
Per proof c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^384 (ROM) and 6 c' (t + k_q)^3 / 2^384 (QROM), summed over N = 20,000 proofs; b = 48 bytes is the length of every digest the transcript writes (SG26 Section I.1: challenge-input keys, leaf and node digests, the written-back stream prefix; at category 1 Keccak-256 keys and trees with SHAKE256 streams in A, SHA-256 keys, BLAKE3 trees and SHAKE256 streams in B; this profile's trees: SHAKE256-384 (A), SHA-384 (B)). Classical: the largest kappa with the tree term <= t / 2^(kappa + 1) for every 1 <= t <= 2^kappa (binding at t = 2^kappa). QROM: the query count at which the tree term reaches 1/2. Revision 10.2: the tree's classical hash level is Theorem TE' of docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md (the hash part taken once for the tree, c'_max (t + N k_q,max)^2 / 2^384), under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1; the per-proof union form is printed beside it as the comparison and is what the proven-basis check uses (the lower figure).

### The hash term of SG26 Theorem 6.6 (2) (revision 10, finding R9-1)

**NON-DEFAULT CONVENTION (T >= K_Q), NOT CERTIFIED** (the summary below uses the every-t hash term; the rows above are not certified).
Per proof c' (t + k_q)^2 / 2^512 (ROM) and 6 c' (t + k_q)^3 / 2^512 (QROM), summed over N = 20,000 proofs; b = 64 bytes is the length of every digest the transcript writes (SG26 Section I.1: challenge-input keys, leaf and node digests, the written-back stream prefix; at category 1 Keccak-256 keys and trees with SHAKE256 streams in A, SHA-256 keys, BLAKE3 trees and SHAKE256 streams in B; this profile's trees: SHAKE256-512 (A), SHA-512 (B)). Classical: the largest kappa with the tree term <= t / 2^(kappa + 1) for every 1 <= t <= 2^kappa (binding at t = 2^kappa). QROM: the query count at which the tree term reaches 1/2. Revision 10.2: the tree's classical hash level is Theorem TE' of docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md (the hash part taken once for the tree, c'_max (t + N k_q,max)^2 / 2^512), under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1; the per-proof union form is printed beside it as the comparison and is what the proven-basis check uses (the lower figure).

### What "proven" and "certified" rest on (revision 10.2; docs/what-is-proven.md)

Every figure called proven, and every row labelled certified, rests on the random-oracle model and on the conditions below, some of them OWED, so in the terms of docs/what-is-proven.md it is conditional; every TREE figure (classical and quantum) is in addition conditional on the recursion heuristic C2, read as a joint probability (never a conditional one; equivalence tests do not discharge it), and none is an unconditional theorem. Conditions: (1) C2, the recursion heuristic (the event 'a child proof accepted by the in-circuit verifier and rejected by the native verifier' does not occur; NOT dischargeable by any random-oracle proof; excluded in practice by in-circuit / native verifier equivalence, a tested engineering property; it enters Theorem TE' at the child's acceptance and by keeping the node relation oracle-free); (2) K-A and K-B, OWED: the round-by-round KNOWLEDGE soundness of both IOPs outside the openings; (3) T-1, OWED from the builders: the transcripts' domain separation across systems (H-DS, injective encodings), their fit to Sharp-Grubbs Protocol 6.5, and the reported c' and k_q (until then c' and k_q are estimates, marked E); (3a) C-4, the level and proof-count binding in node statements: met by design, by search, NOT audited (an audit owed); (3b) H-BIND, collision resistance of the concrete statement-digest functions computed inside the node relations (a standard-model assumption, not an oracle property; it excludes SHAPE-VIOLATION and bounds the tree's node count); (4) the modelling assumptions MA-1 (Keccak-256 and SHAKE256 in A, SHA-256 and SHAKE256 in B, as one random oracle with four disjoint parts) and MA-2' (BLAKE3 derive_key, B's leaves and nodes, as that oracle's leaf and node parts); (5) Sharp-Grubbs, ePrint 2026/2615, Theorem 6.6 (2) and Theorem I.16 (1), (2): a PREPRINT; (6) Theorem TE' (docs/lemma-tree-extraction.md revision 3; revisions 1 and 2 refereed, pass with conditions; revision 3, with SHAPE-VIOLATION and Lemma TE.3, UNREFEREED); (7) Lemma QC (the continuation after a database measurement, from Chiesa-Manohar-Spooner, ePrint 2019/834, Lemma 3.2): refereed, pass (docs/qc-and-status-referee.md); (8) Theorem D (system B's repeated openings): refereed, pass with conditions. Candidate (Johnson-regime) rows rest in addition on DKT26 (Dao, Kominers, Thaler, ePrint 2026/2056), a PREPRINT, and are never certified. At category 1 (256-bit digests) the tree's classical hash level is 121.89 bits (Theorem TE', under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1); the per-proof union form, 114.74, is printed beside it and is the figure the proven-basis check uses; the tables give each profile's figures. The classical hash part is certified on condition H's attack rule unless the basis printed says proven. The tree's QROM level claimed is the per-proof union (69.58 A / 70.45 B at category 1); the one-table form (76.72 / 77.60, hash part 80.40) is printed beside it, under C2, K-A, K-B, T-1. The tree figures are for ONE output tree (attempts = 1; R10-10).
